This has been a really thorough walkthrough, and I'm genuinely happy with all nine of those areas — they cover a lot of what I came in wanting. Before you go off and build, though, let me make sure the scope has a couple of things I'd consider essential, because I don't want to discover they're missing later.

The big one: in all of this we've built saving, searching, organizing, and tidying — but I don't think we ever confirmed the most basic thing I'd do every day. When I spot a saved bookmark in my library and click it, I'd expect it to actually take me to the original webpage. That's the whole reason I'm saving these in the first place. Can you confirm that opening a saved link and landing on the real site is part of what you'll build?

Two smaller things I'd want to be sure are in scope, since my library is going to grow:

- Being able to put my list in an order that helps me — like newest first, or by title — rather than being stuck with one fixed arrangement.
- When I'm tidying up, being able to pick several bookmarks at once and do the same thing to all of them — say, tag them together, or archive a batch — instead of clicking through them one at a time.

If those are covered, then yes, I'm happy for you to start building. If any of them isn't in your plan, I'd like to sort that out first.
